latent_mechanisms.display_name: Aberrant Th2 / Tfh / IL-4 / IL-13 axis activity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Skewed CD4+ T-helper response (Th2 and follicular helper) producing IL-4, IL-13, IL-5; drives IgG4 class switching, eosinophilia, IgE elevation; central upstream driver in IgG4-RD.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Aberrant Treg / IL-10 / TGF-β axis activity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Expanded regulatory T-cell signaling with IL-10 (further driving IgG4 class switch) and TGF-β (driving fibroblast activation and storiform fibrosis).
Oligoclonal CD19+CD27+CD38hi plasmablast expansion in blood; correlates with disease activity better than serum IgG4 in many cases; reservoir for tissue plasma cells.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: CD4+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte tissue infiltration
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Clonally expanded SLAMF7+ CD4+ CTLs producing IFN-γ, IL-1β, TGF-β1; key tissue effector driving inflammation and fibrosis.
Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate enriched in IgG4+ plasma cells (>10/HPF and IgG4/IgG ratio >40%); pathologic hallmark of IgG4-RD.
Activated fibroblast/myofibroblast-driven dense storiform collagen deposition; histologic hallmark; drives irreversible tumefactive masses and organ dysfunction.
Lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with luminal occlusion of medium-sized veins; histologic hallmark contributing to ischemia and fibrosis.
Mass-like organ enlargement that mimics malignancy radiologically and clinically; central diagnostic challenge.
Peripheral eosinophilia, IgE elevation, atopic background commonly accompanying disease; tissue eosinophil infiltration adds to classic histologic picture.

Diffuse sausage-shape pancreatic enlargement with capsule-like rim, irregular narrowing of main pancreatic duct; obstructive jaundice via intrapancreatic CBD compression and new-onset diabetes from islet destruction.
Concentric biliary wall thickening with multifocal strictures, often distal CBD or hilar; mimics PSC and cholangiocarcinoma; produces obstructive cholestasis.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: IgG4-related lacrimal/salivary gland disease (Mikulicz / Küttner tumor)
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Bilateral, painless, persistent enlargement of lacrimal, parotid, and submandibular glands with sicca symptoms; classic Mikulicz/Küttner presentation.
Orbital pseudotumor, dacryoadenitis, extraocular muscle involvement, and infraorbital nerve enlargement causing proptosis, restricted motility, and diplopia.
Periaortic and periureteral soft-tissue rind encasing ureters and great vessels; produces back/flank pain, ureteral obstruction, hydronephrosis, post-renal AKI.
Interstitial plasma cell infiltrate with tubular atrophy and storiform fibrosis; bilateral cortical low-density lesions on imaging; rising creatinine, mild proteinuria, hypocomplementemia.
Mural and periadventitial inflammation/fibrosis of large vessels (aorta, iliacs, coronaries); chronic medial weakening predisposes to aneurysm formation and dissection.
Solid nodules, mass-like consolidation, ground-glass opacities, peribronchovascular interstitial thickening, hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy, pleural thickening.
Diffuse or nodular dural thickening, predominantly of cranial/spinal dura, producing chronic headache, cranial neuropathies (especially II, V, VII, VIII), and rarely venous sinus compression.
Pituitary stalk thickening and gland enlargement with anterior and/or posterior pituitary dysfunction; central diabetes insipidus, hypopituitarism.
Stony-hard fibrosing thyroid mass extending into cervical structures; compressive symptoms (dysphagia, hoarseness, stridor); often associated with primary hypothyroidism.
Consumption of C3/C4 mediated by IgG1/IgG3 in tissue; especially associated with renal (TIN, MGN) and pancreatic involvement; marks active and relapse-prone disease.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Irreversible fibrosis-driven organ functional failure propensity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Late-phase fibrotic remodeling that no longer reverses with immunosuppression; causes pancreatic exocrine/endocrine insufficiency, biliary cirrhosis, renal atrophy, etc.
Tendency to flare on glucocorticoid taper or after withdrawal; higher with multi-organ involvement, very high baseline IgG4, elevated plasmablasts, low complement, prior relapses.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: IL-4 and Tfh-driven germinal center reactions and IL-21 signaling drive B-cell differentiation into IgG4-class plasmablasts.
IL-10 promotes IgG4 class switching from IgG1/IgG3 in B cells, biasing plasmablast output toward IgG4.
TGF-β drives fibroblast proliferation, myofibroblast differentiation, and dense storiform collagen deposition.
IL-5 from Th2/ILC2 cells drives eosinophil maturation and tissue trafficking; IL-4/IL-13 drives IgE class switch.
Circulating plasmablasts traffic to tissue and mature into long-lived IgG4+ plasma cells, producing local IgG4 plasma cell infiltrate.
SLAMF7+ CD4+CTL secrete IFN-γ, IL-1β, and TGF-β1 directly activating fibroblasts; key effector for fibrogenic remodeling.
Dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate plus interstitial expansion produces grossly tumefactive enlargement of involved organ.
Storiform collagen deposition adds firm mass-like component to tumefactive lesions, producing cancer-mimicking imaging appearance.
Venous occlusion produces local ischemia and stromal injury that recruits fibroblasts and reinforces fibrogenic remodeling.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: if pancreas is one of the involved organs
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Tumefactive expansion in the pancreas manifests as type 1 AIP with diffuse sausage-shape enlargement.
Pancreatic head enlargement and contiguous biliary tree inflammation frequently coexist; ~70% of AIP have biliary involvement.
Diffuse parenchymal infiltration produces sausage-shape pancreatic enlargement with smooth contour and capsule-like rim.
Periductal lymphoplasmacytic infiltration produces long-segment irregular narrowing of the main pancreatic duct (vs. focal stricture in malignancy).
Peripheral hypoenhancing capsule-like rim is a relatively specific imaging sign of type 1 AIP.
Islet inflammation and parenchymal damage produce new-onset or worsening diabetes; ~40-70% of AIP patients have abnormal glucose handling at presentation.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: modest elevation; typically lower than acute pancreatitis
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Pancreatic inflammation can elevate lipase, but classic AIP often presents with normal or only mildly elevated lipase despite extensive imaging changes.
Concentric mural infiltration produces multifocal biliary strictures (distal CBD most common, also intrahepatic and hilar).
Strictures upstream of the obstruction produce intrahepatic biliary dilation visible on cross-sectional imaging and MRCP.
Distal CBD compression (often by pancreatic head) and proximal stricture cause CBD dilation upstream.
Cholestatic pattern of liver injury with disproportionate ALP and GGT elevation precedes bilirubin rise.
Mechanical biliary obstruction produces conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and obstructive jaundice.
Painless obstructive jaundice is a classic presentation of IgG4-related cholangitis/AIP.
Multifocal strictures progressively narrow biliary tree, producing risk of cholangitis and persistent obstruction requiring stenting.
Bilateral painless lacrimal gland enlargement is a hallmark of Mikulicz disease.
Bilateral submandibular gland enlargement (Küttner tumor) is highly characteristic and frequently the most prominent salivary site.
Painless parotid enlargement, often bilateral, with relatively preserved gland function early in disease.
Chronic glandular destruction reduces saliva production producing dry mouth, though typically less severe than primary Sjögren.
Lacrimal gland infiltration reduces tear production causing dry eyes, often less symptomatic than primary Sjögren.
Orbital fat, extraocular muscle, and infraorbital nerve involvement produces a mass-like orbital lesion mimicking lymphoma.
Mass effect from orbital infiltration produces unilateral or bilateral proptosis.
Periaortic and periureteric soft-tissue rind on CT/MRI is the imaging hallmark of IgG4-related retroperitoneal fibrosis.
Dull, persistent low-back, flank, or abdominal pain is the most common symptom of retroperitoneal fibrosis.
Encasement of ureters by retroperitoneal soft tissue rind produces uni- or bilateral hydronephrosis with medial deviation of ureters.
Progressive ureteral encasement produces post-renal AKI requiring urgent decompression with stenting or nephrostomy.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: post-renal AKI from bilateral ureteral obstruction
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Bilateral hydronephrosis from ureteral encasement produces obstructive uropathy and rising creatinine.
Bilateral cortical low-density nodular or wedge-shaped lesions on contrast CT are characteristic imaging finding of IgG4-related TIN.
Tubulointerstitial inflammation reduces GFR producing rising creatinine, often subacute and asymptomatic.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: low-grade tubular proteinuria; nephrotic-range only when membranous GN coexists
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Tubular injury produces low-grade proteinuria; coexisting IgG4-related membranous GN can cause nephrotic-range proteinuria.
Immune complex consumption (often classical pathway) lowers C3, especially in patients with renal or pancreatic involvement.
C4 consumption reflects classical pathway activation and is a frequent and earlier marker of activity than C3 in IgG4-RD.
Persistent hypocomplementemia despite treatment marks ongoing subclinical activity and predicts relapse on steroid taper.
Periaortic soft-tissue cuff visible on CT/MRI/PET represents inflammatory and fibrotic remodeling of vessel adventitia.
Chronic medial inflammation and fibrotic weakening of aortic wall predispose to aneurysmal dilation, especially infrarenal abdominal aorta.
Medial weakening and aneurysmal change predispose to dissection or rupture; uncommon but high-mortality complication.
Solid nodules and mass-like consolidations are common pulmonary manifestations and may mimic primary lung cancer.
Mass-like consolidation pattern is one of four classic radiologic types of IgG4-related lung disease.
Hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy mimicking sarcoidosis or lymphoma is common in IgG4-related lung disease.
Diffuse or focal dural thickening with avid contrast enhancement on MRI is the imaging hallmark of IgG4-related pachymeningitis.
Compressive or infiltrative damage to cranial nerves at skull base causes optic, trigeminal, facial, and vestibulocochlear neuropathies.
Pituitary stalk thickening and gland enlargement on MRI are imaging hallmarks of IgG4-related hypophysitis.
Stony-hard fibrosing thyroid mass with extension into surrounding cervical tissues defines Riedel-type involvement.
Flow cytometric quantification of CD19+CD27+CD38hi plasmablasts directly measures the underlying mechanism and tracks disease activity better than serum IgG4.
Pathology counts of IgG4+ plasma cells per HPF (with organ-specific thresholds, e.g., ≥10–50/HPF) directly reflect this mechanism.
IgG4+/IgG+ plasma cell ratio >40% on tissue is a major histologic criterion in the consensus diagnostic framework.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: elevated in ~60-90% of cases; ~10-30% IgG4-seronegative despite biopsy-proven disease
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Plasmablast and plasma cell IgG4 production raises serum IgG4 above normal range (>135 mg/dL); high specificity at very high levels but moderate sensitivity.
IgG4 is a subclass of IgG; substantial elevation of IgG4 raises total IgG modestly.
Peripheral eosinophilia (>500/μL) is present in approximately 30-40% of IgG4-RD patients reflecting Th2/IL-5 activity.
IL-4-driven IgE class switching elevates serum IgE in a substantial proportion of patients, especially those with atopic background.
Tissue eosinophil infiltration accompanies plasma cell-rich infiltrate and is one of the supportive but non-specific histologic features.
IgG4-related lymphadenopathy is common, often generalized, with multiple histologic patterns mimicking Castleman, MALT lymphoma, or angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma.
Established storiform fibrosis is largely irreversible; cumulative damage produces pancreatic insufficiency, biliary cirrhosis, renal atrophy, hypopituitarism, etc.
Relapse occurs in 30-50% within 3 years of glucocorticoid monotherapy; risk higher with multi-organ disease, very high IgG4, low complement, atopy.
Pancreatic islet damage produces new-onset DM in a high proportion of AIP patients; pre-existing DM frequently worsens.

Pancreatic head mass, hilar biliary stricture, orbital mass, lung mass, retroperitoneal mass, lymphadenopathy all radiologically mimic malignancy and may lead to unnecessary surgery without histologic confirmation.
End-organ failure (renal, hepatic, pancreatic), aortic catastrophe, and complications of long-term immunosuppression contribute to excess mortality.
Aortic dissection and rupture are leading causes of disease-specific mortality in patients with vascular involvement.
Sustained antigen presentation drives expansion of clonal CD4+CTLs alongside Th2/Tfh activity in chronic IgG4-RD pathogenesis.
Periphlebitic lymphoplasmacytic infiltration progressively occludes medium-sized veins producing obliterative phlebitis.
Tumefactive expansion in retroperitoneum manifests as periaortic and periureteral soft-tissue rind.
Tumefactive infiltration of orbital fat, lacrimal gland, and extraocular muscles produces orbital pseudotumor.
Tumefactive dural thickening, often skull base or spinal, produces compressive symptoms.
Bilateral exocrine gland enlargement produces classic Mikulicz/Küttner phenotype.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: if aorta or large vessels involved
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Periadventitial tumefactive cuff manifests as periaortitis with risk of aneurysm formation.
Pituitary stalk and gland infiltration produces hypophysitis with anterior and/or posterior pituitary dysfunction.
Tumefactive renal cortical infiltration produces TIN with low-density imaging lesions.
Renal involvement is the strongest clinical predictor of marked hypocomplementemia in IgG4-RD.

axes.shape_free_text: Low baseline; rises with vascular catastrophe (dissection), advanced organ failure, infection from immunosuppression, and rare malignancy progression.
Normal <135 mg/dL. Elevated in ~60-90% of patients at diagnosis; very high values (>500-700) increase specificity. Can be normal in active biopsy-proven disease (~10-30%).
Often modestly elevated (1500-3000 mg/dL); polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia common.
Useful when total IgG also elevated; ratio > 0.08-0.10 supportive of IgG4-RD.
Often elevated, especially in patients with atopic background; correlates with eosinophilia and Th2 activity.
Normal typically <900 cells/mL. Markedly elevated (often >3000-5000) at active disease; correlates with activity better than IgG4 in many cohorts. Drops rapidly with rituximab or steroids.
Normal up to ~0.5; mild-to-moderate elevation in ~30-40%; rarely hypereosinophilic.
Normal ~80-180 mg/dL. May be low especially with renal or pancreatic involvement; persistent low C3 portends relapse.
Normal ~15-50 mg/dL. Often falls earlier and more profoundly than C3; persistent low C4 predicts relapse.
Frequently elevated (often disproportionately to CRP); reflects polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia rather than acute inflammation.
Often only mildly elevated despite tumefactive disease; striking ESR/CRP dissociation is common.
Low-titer ANA positive in ~30-40%; nonspecific.
Low-titer RF can be positive in a minority; nonspecific.
May rise from intrinsic TIN, IgG4-related membranous GN, or post-renal obstruction from retroperitoneal fibrosis.
Low-grade tubular proteinuria typical of TIN; nephrotic-range when membranous GN coexists.
Microhematuria possible; not a dominant feature.
Cholestatic pattern with ALP and GGT elevation reflects sclerosing cholangitis; rises before bilirubin.
Elevated in obstructive jaundice from intrapancreatic CBD compression or distal/hilar stricture.
Mildly elevated in cholestatic injury; markedly elevated only with acute biliary obstruction.
Mildly elevated in cholestatic injury.
Often only mildly elevated in AIP despite extensive imaging changes; high values suggest superimposed acute pancreatitis or alternative diagnosis.
Often only mildly elevated in AIP, similar to lipase.
Elevated in patients with new-onset or worsening diabetes from islet damage in AIP.
Elevated in proportion to duration and severity of pancreatic islet damage.
Usually normal; mildly elevated only with cholangitis or steroid effect.
Mild normocytic anemia of chronic disease common in active multi-organ involvement.
Typically normal or mildly increased; no consistent abnormality.
Usually afebrile; low-grade fever uncommon in pure IgG4-RD; high-grade fever should prompt search for infection or alternative diagnosis.
Organ-specific cutoffs (e.g., ≥10/HPF salivary, ≥30/HPF lacrimal/lung, ≥50/HPF pancreas/kidney/lymph node) used in 2019 ACR/EULAR classification.
>40% supportive of IgG4-RD; near 100% achievable in classic cases.
Pathologic hallmark; cartwheel pattern of fibrosis on H&E. One of three major histologic features.
Lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with luminal occlusion of medium-sized veins.
Supportive but non-specific histologic feature; not always present.
Lymphadenopathy is common (~40-60%), often generalized, and can be the presenting feature.
Painless, often bilateral cervical, mediastinal, hilar, axillary, retroperitoneal nodal enlargement.
Hilar/mediastinal nodal enlargement; sarcoidosis-like distribution possible.
Sausage-shaped diffuse pancreatic enlargement with smooth contour and loss of lobulation; the imaging hallmark of type 1 AIP.
Long-segment (>1/3 length) irregular narrowing of main pancreatic duct with skip lesions; vs. focal abrupt cut-off in malignancy.
Peripheral hypoenhancing capsule-like rim around enlarged pancreas; relatively specific imaging sign.
Multifocal smooth concentric strictures (distal CBD most common, also intrahepatic and hilar); concentric mural thickening on cross-section.
Upstream dilation from strictures, often hilar.
Dilated upstream of distal stricture caused by intrapancreatic CBD compression or distal/hilar inflammation.
Symmetric, painless, persistent enlargement of bilateral lacrimal glands; may produce lid fullness and S-shaped eyelid contour.
Bilateral, hard, painless enlargement (Küttner tumor); often the most prominent salivary site.
Bilateral painless parotid enlargement.
Dry mouth from glandular destruction; often less severe than primary Sjögren.
Dry eyes from lacrimal involvement; often subjectively milder than primary Sjögren.
Mass-like infiltration of orbital fat, extraocular muscles, and infraorbital nerve enlargement (a relatively specific MRI finding).
Unilateral or bilateral proptosis with restriction of motility.
Periaortic and periureteric soft-tissue mantle on CT/MRI, often FDG-avid; medial deviation of ureters.
Dull, persistent low-back, flank, or abdominal pain typical of retroperitoneal fibrosis.
Uni- or bilateral hydronephrosis from ureteral encasement by retroperitoneal fibrosis.
Bilateral cortical low-density nodular or wedge-shaped lesions on contrast CT; characteristic of IgG4-related TIN.
Periaortic soft-tissue cuff (>3 mm) on CT/MRI; typically infrarenal aorta or thoracic aorta; FDG-avid on PET.
Late-stage finding from chronic medial weakening; abdominal aorta most common.
Solid nodules; one of four classic radiologic types of IgG4-related lung disease.
Mass-like consolidation; one of four classic radiologic patterns; mimics primary lung cancer.
Pleural thickening or effusion possible.
Diffuse or nodular dural thickening with avid contrast enhancement on MRI; often skull base or spinal.
Optic, trigeminal, facial, vestibulocochlear deficits from skull-base infiltration or hypertrophic pachymeningitis.
Pituitary stalk thickening and/or gland enlargement; central diabetes insipidus and hypopituitarism may follow.
Stony-hard fibrosing thyroid gland extending into cervical structures; produces compressive dysphagia and hoarseness.
Mild splenomegaly possible; not a dominant feature.
Vague abdominal discomfort common in AIP/cholangitis; severe pain unusual unless complicated.
Painless obstructive jaundice is a classic presentation of AIP/cholangitis; may be intermittent.
Modest unintentional weight loss common; significant weight loss should prompt malignancy workup.
Common nonspecific symptom.
New-onset DM or worsening of pre-existing DM in patients with pancreatic involvement; ~40-70% at diagnosis of AIP.
Personal history of asthma, allergic rhinitis, eczema in ~30-40%; correlates with eosinophilia and IgE elevation.
Number of involved organs at presentation; predicts relapse risk and treatment intensity.
IgG4-RD Responder Index (RI) — a composite organ-by-organ activity and damage score (0-3 per organ) used in trials and clinical follow-up.
Rapid clinical and radiologic response to prednisolone (within 2-4 weeks) is characteristic; partial response is a red flag for alternative diagnosis.

Probability that the clinical picture also fits a competing malignant differential (pancreatic adenocarcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, lymphoma, primary lung cancer); always considered in pre-treatment workup.
0 not started, 1 induction full dose, 2 active taper, 3 low-dose maintenance or off therapy. Relapse risk highest in transitions 2→3.
Modest excess risk of cancers (lung, pancreatic, lymphoma) particularly in the first 1-2 years; debate persists about whether disease itself or surveillance bias drives signal.
Risk of progressive obstructive jaundice or cholangitis from worsening strictures.
Progressive ureteral obstruction from retroperitoneal fibrosis requiring stent or nephrostomy.
High risk of new-onset DM in active AIP, especially diffuse pancreatic involvement.
Rare but high-mortality complication in patients with periaortitis and aneurysmal change.
Cumulative risk of ESRD (TIN), pancreatic insufficiency, biliary cirrhosis, hypopituitarism with delayed treatment.
30-50% relapse within 3 years on glucocorticoid monotherapy; higher with multi-organ disease, very high IgG4, low complement.
Iatrogenic from glucocorticoids and B-cell depletion; Pneumocystis, varicella reactivation, hepatitis B reactivation, tuberculosis.
Risk during rituximab therapy in HBV-exposed patients; mandates HBV screening and antiviral prophylaxis when indicated.
Reactivation risk under prolonged glucocorticoids and B-cell depletion; pre-treatment screening important.
Hyperglycemia, weight gain, mood changes, osteoporosis, infection risk; major drivers of long-term morbidity.
Rituximab infusion reaction risk during initial cycle; mitigated by premedication and slow titration.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Both consumed via classical-pathway immune complex activation; C4 typically falls earlier and more profoundly than C3.
IgG4 is a subclass; substantial elevation contributes to and is correlated with total IgG hypergammaglobulinemia.
Plasmablast count tracks total disease activity better than serum IgG4; rises and falls with response.
Both are downstream of IL-4/IL-5 Th2 signaling; co-elevation supports atopic-rich phenotype.
ESR elevation in IgG4-RD is largely driven by polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia rather than acute inflammation.
Pancreatic head enlargement compresses intrapancreatic CBD producing distal stricture and upstream biliary dilation.
Periureteric fibrotic mantle progressively encases ureters producing hydronephrosis.
Bilateral ureteral obstruction produces post-renal AKI.
Biliary obstruction produces cholestatic enzyme elevation that precedes hyperbilirubinemia.
ALP elevation typically precedes the rise in conjugated bilirubin in cholestatic syndromes.
Persistent low complement during taper is an established predictor of relapse, especially with renal involvement.
Plasmablasts that fail to fully suppress on therapy or rebound during taper presage clinical relapse.
Multi-organ disease at baseline is a robust predictor of relapse.
Very high baseline serum IgG4 (>4-fold ULN) and IgG4 levels that fail to normalize on therapy associate with higher relapse risk.
Atopic background and eosinophil-rich phenotype associate with relapse propensity.
Chronic adventitial inflammation and medial weakening drive aneurysmal dilation over years.
Larger aneurysm diameter monotonically increases dissection/rupture risk.
Diffuse parenchymal involvement causes more islet damage and higher likelihood of new-onset DM.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Empirical steroids must not be given when malignancy (pancreatic adenocarcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, lymphoma) cannot be reasonably excluded; tissue diagnosis preferred first.
Active untreated infection should be controlled before initiating high-dose immunosuppression.
Late-stage fibrotic disease responds less completely; reversal of established fibrosis is limited.

side_effects.interpretation: Steroid-induced hyperglycemia, particularly in patients with AIP-related DM
Mood changes, hyperglycemia, weight gain, osteoporosis with prolonged use
Increased infection risk, especially with prolonged maintenance

treatments.context_specific_role: Standard induction therapy. Typical induction: prednisolone 0.6-0.8 mg/kg/day (~30-40 mg/day) for 2-4 weeks then taper over 3-6 months; many regimens continue low-dose maintenance (2.5-5 mg/day) for 1-3 years to reduce relapse, especially in Japanese practice. Rapid clinical and radiologic response within 2-4 weeks supports diagnosis.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Mandatory pre-treatment HBV screening and antiviral prophylaxis for HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ patients; risk of fulminant reactivation.
Plasmablast-driven disease responds particularly well to B-cell depletion.

failure_modes: Re-expansion of plasmablasts after B-cell recovery (~6-12 months)
Relapse despite B-cell depletion in fibrotic-dominant disease

side_effects.interpretation: First-dose infusion reaction; mitigated with premedication and slow titration
Hypogammaglobulinemia and infections especially with repeated cycles
Hepatitis B reactivation in HBV-exposed patients without prophylaxis

treatments.context_specific_role: Used for refractory disease, relapsed disease, steroid-intolerant patients, and as first-line in selected patients with high-risk phenotypes (e.g., extensive multi-organ disease, severe pancreatobiliary disease). Typical regimen: 1000 mg × 2 doses 2 weeks apart, or 375 mg/m² × 4 weekly. Maintenance dosing every 6 months considered for high-risk relapse phenotypes.

Steroid-sparing agent for maintenance, particularly in resource-limited settings or when rituximab unavailable. Typical dose 2-2.5 mg/kg/day. Less robust evidence than for vasculitides; some centers prefer mycophenolate or methotrexate.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Mycophenolate is teratogenic; effective contraception or alternative agent required.

treatments.context_specific_role: Steroid-sparing maintenance alternative to azathioprine; typical dose 1.0-1.5 g BID.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Methotrexate accumulates in renal impairment with severe toxicity.

treatments.context_specific_role: Steroid-sparing maintenance alternative; weekly oral or SC dosing 10-20 mg.

treatments.drug_class: Selective estrogen receptor modulator (used historically for retroperitoneal fibrosis)
failure_modes: Largely supplanted by glucocorticoids and rituximab
treatments.context_specific_role: Historic adjunct for retroperitoneal fibrosis when glucocorticoids contraindicated or as steroid-sparing in idiopathic RPF; rarely used as primary therapy in modern IgG4-RD management.
Emerging targeted therapy with broader B-cell lineage coverage than rituximab (CD19 expressed on plasmablasts); positive phase 3 data (MITIGATE trial) in IgG4-RD reported in 2024-2025.

Indicated when severe obstructive jaundice, cholangitis, or diagnostic uncertainty (with bile/brush cytology) precedes definitive medical therapy. Typically removed after steroid-induced stricture resolution.

failure_modes: Need for repeated exchange until immunosuppressive therapy reverses fibrosis
treatments.context_specific_role: Required for relief of obstructive uropathy when bilateral hydronephrosis or AKI present; bridge to medical therapy.
Required for AIP-related and steroid-induced DM; insulin often necessary during high-dose steroid induction.

failure_modes: Inadequate symptom relief if structural disease severe
treatments.context_specific_role: For exocrine pancreatic insufficiency from chronic AIP-related parenchymal damage with steatorrhea, weight loss, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency.

male.trajectory_modulation: Male predominance most pronounced in type 1 AIP, retroperitoneal fibrosis, aortitis, and pancreatobiliary disease (3-8:1 in AIP). Mikulicz/Küttner more balanced; orbital and head-and-neck disease more equal across sexes.

above_60.trajectory_modulation: Peak incidence in 50s-70s; pediatric IgG4-RD is rare and usually presents with orbital or salivary disease.

japanese.trajectory_modulation: AIP first defined in Japan; reported prevalence highest in Japan, Korea, China; HLA-DRB1*0405 and DQB1*0401 associations described in Japanese cohorts.

present.trajectory_modulation: Asthma, allergic rhinitis, atopic dermatitis, food allergy more common in IgG4-RD patients; correlates with eosinophilia, IgE elevation, and possibly higher relapse risk.

carrier.trajectory_modulation: Reported association with type 1 AIP in Japanese cohorts; effect size modest.

present.trajectory_modulation: Some series suggest enrichment among workers exposed to industrial dusts and solvents, especially in retroperitoneal fibrosis and pulmonary phenotypes.

current_or_former.trajectory_modulation: Smoking associated with retroperitoneal fibrosis (especially idiopathic RPF) and possibly pulmonary IgG4-RD.

supportive_care: PJP prophylaxis (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole) during prolonged high-dose glucocorticoids and especially with rituximab
HBV screening (HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs) before rituximab; entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis for HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ patients
Latent TB screening (IGRA or TST) before sustained immunosuppression; INH prophylaxis if positive

Vaccination optimization before/during therapy: pneumococcal (PCV20 or PCV15+PPSV23), influenza annually, COVID-19, recombinant zoster, Tdap, HBV; live vaccines avoided during active immunosuppression
Bone protection: calcium and vitamin D, baseline DEXA, bisphosphonate or denosumab for steroid-induced osteoporosis prevention
Glycemic monitoring: HbA1c at baseline and periodically; finger-stick glucose at home during steroid induction and taper
Cardiovascular risk monitoring: blood pressure, lipids, weight; routine aortic imaging surveillance for patients with periaortitis
Tissue biopsy before empirical steroids whenever feasible to exclude malignancy mimics (pancreatic adenocarcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, lymphoma)
Multidisciplinary follow-up imaging (MRI/MRCP for pancreatobiliary, CT/MRI for retroperitoneal/aortic, MRI brain for pachymeningitis/hypophysitis) to assess response and detect new organ involvement
Disease activity monitoring with serum IgG4, IgG4/IgG ratio, complement (C3, C4), peripheral plasmablast count (when available), eosinophils, IgE, and IgG4-RD Responder Index
Patient education on relapse symptoms (return of jaundice, gland swelling, flank pain, new neurologic symptoms, vision change) for early reassessment

Endocrine replacement: levothyroxine for hypothyroidism (Riedel/autoimmune thyroiditis); desmopressin for central DI; physiologic glucocorticoid and other anterior pituitary replacement for hypophysitis
Pancreatic enzyme replacement and fat-soluble vitamin (A, D, E, K) supplementation for exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
Cancer surveillance during the first 1-2 years after diagnosis given modest excess malignancy signal in some cohorts
Genetic counseling and contraception planning when teratogenic agents (mycophenolate, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide) are considered
Dental, ophthalmologic, and ENT follow-up for sicca symptoms; artificial tears and saliva substitutes; dental caries surveillance
Psychosocial support and patient advocacy resources given rarity, diagnostic delay, and chronicity of the disease
